intro.opening: Three hours on the Nile at Aswan in a felucca, Egypt's traditional lateen-rigged sailing boat. This is a sailing experience, not a sightseeing tour: no temples to enter, no ticket queues. You watch the Corniche slide past, track the birds above the river and let the wind do the work.
intro.whyThisOrder: The boat is privately yours, so it can drift longer around the islands or turn back early. Feluccas move with the wind, which at Aswan is generally reliable but never hurried. From October through April temperatures are moderate and the northerly breeze is consistent; from May onward, morning sails are noticeably cooler than afternoon ones.
intro.returnNote: Back at the docking point on the Corniche roughly three hours after embarkation

lunch.text: Optional Nile Feast package, on board or at a riverside restaurant, chosen at booking

fitFor: have already seen, or will see, Philae, the High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk, and want one unstructured morning or afternoon that belongs to the river
are travelling alone or as a small party: the sail takes bookings from a single person upward, with no minimum group
are travelling as a family: there's no minimum age
worthKnowing: A felucca has no shade canopy. It's an open boat on open water, so plan around young children and sun exposure.
It isn't a fast-moving trip. If you're travelling with restless children or need structured commentary throughout, temper your expectations.
There are no temples to enter on this sail.
In May and June the heat intensifies and the wind can be variable. Morning departures are significantly more comfortable in the warmer months.
intro.closingLine: Three hours on a felucca is the quietest argument for noticing.

stops.title: Pickup and transfer to the Aswan Corniche
stops.text: A short transfer from your agreed meeting point to the Corniche, the broad riverside promenade on the east bank. Your English-speaking assistant meets you there and walks you down to the felucca.

stops.title: Sailing on the Nile
stops.text: A traditional wooden-hulled boat with a single triangular sail. You pass the riverbanks on both sides, palm-fringed islands mid-channel and Aswan's rocky shoreline, while the assistant talks about the felucca's place in Egyptian life. Ask questions, or say nothing at all.

stops.title: Nile Feast lunch, if you've chosen it
stops.text: Served at about the midpoint of the sail, on board or at a riverside restaurant. Freshly baked Egyptian bread, baba ghanoush and tahini, then grilled chicken or seasoned meat with aromatic rice and seasonal vegetables. Soft drinks and mineral water come with it.

optional.text: Nile Feast lunch, on board or at a riverside restaurant: optional add-on, chosen at booking

stops.title: Back to the Corniche
stops.text: The return leg follows the same river in reverse, back to the docking point on the Corniche roughly three hours after embarkation.
